Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller films released in 2020. These picks span a range of styles—from gritty neo‑noir to high‑stakes heist dramas—and have earned praise from critics and audiences alike.

| # | Title | Director | Key Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|----------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | A sprawling, time‑juggling saga that blends crime history with Scorsese’s signature storytelling. |
| 2 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | A courtroom thriller that doubles as a political drama, with razor‑sharp dialogue and strong ensemble performances. |
| 3 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie’s fast‑paced, witty take on the British gangster world, with a clever plot twist. |
| 4 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A tense psychological thriller about a man accused of a crime he didn’t commit, featuring powerful performances. |
| 5 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern retelling of the classic horror story that doubles as a crime thriller, with a strong female lead and suspenseful pacing. |
| 6 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A historical crime drama that explores themes of justice and betrayal, with a gripping duel at its core. |
| 7 | **The Nightingale** | Jennifer Kent | Lily James, David Wenham | A gritty, atmospheric thriller set in colonial Australia, blending crime with survival horror. |
| 8 | **The Little Things** | John Lee Hancock | Denzel Washington, Rami Malek, Jared Leto | A noir‑inspired investigation that keeps viewers guessing until the very end. |
| 9 | **The Devil All the Time** | Antonio Campos | Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, Riley Keough | A bleak, atmospheric crime thriller that weaves multiple storylines into a chilling tapestry. |
|10 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern retelling of the classic horror story that doubles as a crime thriller, with a strong female lead and suspenseful pacing. |

### How to Watch

- **Streaming**: Many of these titles are available on major platforms such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu, and HBO Max.  
- **Blu‑ray/DVD**: For collectors, most of these films have physical releases with bonus features.  
- **Rent/Buy**: Digital rental or purchase options are available on iTunes, Google Play, and Vudu.

Enjoy your crime‑thriller marathon! If you’d like more details on any particular film—plot summaries, reviews, or behind‑the‑scenes trivia—just let me know.
